To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the intracellular concentration of alpha-Tocopherol (TocH) is directly correlated with the level of expression of lipoprotein Lipase (LPL), which is a key enzyme in the delivery of triglyceride (TG)-bound TocH to peripheral tissues.
the intracellular levels of the antioxidant vitamin alpha-tocopheral (alpha-Toc) in skeletal muscle are directly dependent on the expression of lipoprotein (LPL) in vivo.
over-expression of lipoprotein-lipase (LPL), a lipolytic enzyme, in skeletal muscle of transgenic mice increases alpha-tocopherols levels in the muscle, but not in the brain or heart.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of lipoprotein metabolism in the delivery of vitamin E to muscle tissue.
the cellular uptake of chylomicrons-located alpha-TocH into skeletal muscle in vivo.
the elucidation of the mechanisms of alpha-TocOH uptake and metabolism in skeletal and cardiac muscle in vivo.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LPL is the key enzyme for the delivery of alpha-TocOH to skeletal muscle.
the uptake of chylomicrons and their remnants in muscle is dependent upon LPL and that this uptake is the primary route for delivery of alpha-TocOH to muscle.
the increased LPL activity in skeletal muscle of the transgenic mouse model leads to increased alpha-TocH concentration and that this is due to increased alpha-TCH delivery to the skeletal muscle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transgenic mouse model presented in this study demonstrates that the cellular uptake of chylomicrone-associated alpha-tocopherols in muscle is directly related to LPL activity in skeletal muscle.
the transgenic mice expressing LPL in muscle have increased levels of alpha-Tocopoherol in muscle, which may protect against lipid peroxidation.

the uptake of chylomicrons-located alpha-TocH is dependent on the level and activity of LPL in skeletal muscle and that the intracellular alpha-TecH levels are positively correlated with the intracellular NEFA levels in skeletal muscle in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LPL is a key regulator of alpha-Tocopherol levels within muscle.
LPL activity in muscle is a key determinant in determining the intramuscular alpha-TocH content.
LPL is an important player in the delivery of alpha-Toc to skeletal muscle.
